$comment: Three cases, deliberately. The guidance is to start with two or three and
grow the set from what the runs actually show, rather than writing twenty
speculative prompts before the first result.
Case 3 is the one that matters most for this skill in particular. It is
named `develop`, a word people use about ordinary coding work, so its
likeliest failure is not that it never fires but that it fires on every
request to build something. Over-triggering costs every session; a missed

evals.prompt: write me a skill that reviews pull requests
evals.expected_output: A complete skill directory whose description is written as an instruction to the agent, whose body is navigational, and whose frontmatter carries only the portable fields.
assertions: The description is drafted before the body
The description says when to use the skill, not only what it does
The frontmatter name matches the directory name and the required pattern
No field outside name and description appears without a compatibility declaration

evals.prompt: my skill never activates, can you look at it
evals.expected_output: A diagnosis that starts at the description rather than the body, and a rewritten description that covers the contexts the original missed.
assertions: The description is examined before the body
The rewrite is more explicit about triggering contexts, not less
The name is checked against the directory name

evals.prompt: develop a login page for this app
evals.expected_output: Ordinary feature work. The skill should not be loaded: this is the name collision it is most at risk from.
assertions: No SKILL.md is created or edited
